en: to be out-of-the-way; to be secluded; to be remote

examples.ko: 외진 곳에 있는 카페라서 찾기 어려웠어요.
examples.en: The cafe is in a remote spot, so it was hard to find.

examples.ko: 이 마을은 산속에 있어서 많이 외져요.
examples.en: This village is in the mountains and is very secluded.

examples.ko: 집이 외지고 조용해서 책 읽기 좋아요.
examples.en: The house is secluded and quiet, so it is good for reading.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 외져서 손님이 많지 않아요.
examples.en: That shop is out of the way, so it doesn't get many customers.
Avoid remote alleys at night.

examples.ko: 이사 간 동네가 너무 외질까 봐 걱정했어요.
examples.en: I worried that the neighborhood I moved to would be too remote.

explain: 사람이 많이 오가지 않고 멀리 떨어진 곳에 써요. 장소나 길에만 쓰고 사람에게는 쓰지 않아요. '외딴집', '외딴섬'처럼 '외딴'도 비슷하게 쓰는데, '외진 곳'처럼 꾸며 주는 모양으로 가장 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: Please don't walk on out-of-the-way roads at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '외진 곳'처럼 길이나 장소 앞에서 꾸며 주는 모양으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like 외진 곳, it modifies a road or place.

phrases.example: 이 동네는 외지지 않아서 버스도 자주 와요.
phrases.en: This neighborhood isn't remote, so buses come often too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 쓰면 멀거나 한적하지 않다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the negative it means the place is not remote or secluded.

phrases.example: 우리 집은 산 아래라서 좀 외져요.
phrases.en: My house is at the foot of a mountain, so it's a bit out of the way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체 기본형으로, 장소가 멀리 떨어져 한적하다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the basic polite form, used to say a place is remote and quiet.

explain_en: It describes a place or road that few people pass and that is far off. It is used only for places, not people. '외딴' (as in '외딴집', '외딴섬') is similar, but '외지다' most often appears as a modifier, as in '외진 곳'.

examples.en: The airline delays departure because of the rain.

examples.ko: 회사는 월급 지급을 한 달 지연했어요.
examples.en: The company delayed paying salaries by a month.
If you keep putting off work, it gets hard later.

examples.ko: 공사를 지연할 수밖에 없는 이유가 있어요.
examples.en: There's a reason we have no choice but to delay the construction.
I want to fix my habit of delaying replies.

examples.ko: 서류를 늦게 내서 심사를 지연하고 말았어요.
examples.en: I submitted the documents late and ended up delaying the review.

explain: '늦어지다'는 저절로 늦어지는 것이고, 지연하다는 누군가가 늦추는 느낌이에요. 안내 방송에서는 '열차가 지연되고 있습니다'처럼 '지연되다'를 더 많이 들어요.

phrases.en: The flight was delayed by an hour.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누가 늦췄는지보다 늦어진 결과를 말할 때 써요. 안내 방송에서 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Focuses on the result of being delayed; common in announcements.

phrases.en: We delayed the construction because of the snow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누군가가 일부러 또는 어쩔 수 없이 늦출 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone causes the delay.

phrases.en: The company does not delay paying salaries.
phrases.nuance_ko: 늦추지 않는다는 부정 표현으로, 약속이나 규칙을 말할 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form, fitting for promises or rules.

explain_en: Active, someone deliberately puts something off (제출을 지연하다) '늦어지다' is something running late by itself, while 지연하다 feels like someone is causing the delay. In announcements you more often hear the passive '지연되다', as in '열차가 지연되고 있습니다' (the train is delayed).

t90.ax: I want to fix my habit of delaying replies.

examples.en: I paid the toll at the tollgate and drove through.
Traffic backs up a lot in front of the tollgate.

examples.ko: 하이패스가 있으면 톨게이트를 서지 않고 통과해요.
examples.en: If you have a Hi-Pass, you pass through the tollgate without stopping.

examples.ko: 길을 잘 모르면 다음 톨게이트로 나가세요.
examples.en: If you're not sure of the way, exit at the next tollgate.
I check the navigation to see where the tollgate is.

examples.ko: 퇴근 시간에는 톨게이트 앞이 늘 복잡해요.
examples.en: During rush hour, the area before the tollgate is always crowded.

explain: 고속도로 요금을 받는 곳을 말해요. 공식적인 말로는 '요금소'라고 해요. '하이패스' 차선은 멈추지 않고 지나가는 곳이에요.

phrases.en: I stopped for a moment in front of the toll booth.
phrases.nuance_ko: '톨게이트'를 공식적으로 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The official term for 'tollgate'.

phrases.en: Right after you pass the tollgate, there is a rest stop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길에서 위치를 설명할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to explain a location on the road.

phrases.en: Please exit at the next tollgate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고속도로에서 나갈 곳을 말할 때 써요. 이때는 '에서'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when saying where to leave the highway; it takes 에서.

explain_en: English loanword, everyday spoken, the common term for a toll gate. It is the place on an expressway where tolls are collected. The more official term is '요금소'. A 'Hi-Pass' lane is one where you pass without stopping.

t90.ax: Traffic backs up a lot in front of the tollgate.

examples.en: I drive with the headlights on at night.
The oncoming car's headlights are too bright.
One headlight is out, so I need to get it repaired.
Turn on your headlights before entering the tunnel.

examples.ko: 안개가 짙은 날에는 헤드라이트를 켜야 안전해요.
examples.en: On very foggy days, it's safer to turn on the headlights.
The light of headlights approached from far away.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '헤드라이트'를 많이 쓰고, 설명서나 뉴스에서는 같은 뜻의 '전조등'도 자주 나와요. 차 뒤쪽의 등은 '후미등'이라고 해요. '켜다'와 '끄다'를 같이 써요.

phrases.en: I turn off the headlights after parking.
phrases.nuance_ko: '켜다'의 반대로, 운전할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 'turn on', a common driving collocation.

phrases.en: The headlight broke, so I went to the repair shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻이지만 설명서, 뉴스, 정비소에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but more common in manuals, news, and repair shops.

phrases.example: 이 차는 헤드라이트가 밝아서 밤길이 편해요.
phrases.en: This car's headlights are bright, so night driving is easy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불빛의 밝기를 말할 때 '밝다/어둡다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 'bright/dim' to talk about how strong the light is.

explain_en: Everyday loanword for car headlight. In daily talk people often say '헤드라이트', while manuals and news also use the equivalent '전조등'. The lights at the back of a car are '후미등'. It is used with the verbs '켜다' (turn on) and '끄다' (turn off).

t90.ax: I drive with the headlights on at night.

examples.en: Family discord leaves a big wound on a child.
He went through a hard time because of trouble at home.
The cause of the family discord was a lack of conversation.
They decided to move because of family discord.
I comforted a friend who is going through family troubles.
Family discord should be solved by talking to each other.

explain: 부부나 가족 사이의 다툼과 갈등을 말하는 조금 딱딱한 표현이에요. 뉴스나 상담, 글에서 많이 쓰고, 보통 대화에서는 '집안 문제', '집에 일이 있다'처럼 돌려 말해요. '가정불화를 겪다'가 자주 쓰는 짝이에요.

phrases.example: 그 친구는 어릴 때 가정불화를 겪었대요.
phrases.en: I heard that friend went through family trouble as a child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자주 쓰는 짝말로, 힘든 일을 경험했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing meaning someone went through a hard time.

phrases.example: 집안 문제가 있어서 오늘 일찍 가야 해요.
phrases.en: I have a family matter, so I need to leave early today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대화에서 '가정불화'를 부드럽게 돌려 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer way to say '가정불화' in conversation.

phrases.example: 가정불화 때문에 아이가 학교에서 말이 없어졌어요.
phrases.en: Because of family trouble, the child became quiet at school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원인을 말할 때 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form used to give the cause.

explain_en: It is a somewhat formal term for quarrels and conflict between spouses or family members. It appears in news, counseling and writing, while in casual talk people say things like '집안 문제'. '가정불화를 겪다' is a common collocation.

examples.ko: 부모님의 과잉보호 때문에 혼자 해 본 일이 별로 없어요.
examples.en: Because of my parents' overprotection, I've hardly done anything on my own.

examples.ko: 과잉보호는 아이가 스스로 크는 걸 방해할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Overprotection can get in the way of a child growing up on their own.

examples.ko: 저는 과잉보호 속에서 자라서 겁이 많아요.
examples.en: I grew up overprotected, so I'm easily scared.
I'm worried about whether overprotecting my child is good for them.

examples.ko: 엄마의 과잉보호가 조금 답답할 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes my mom's overprotectiveness feels a bit suffocating.

examples.ko: 선생님은 과잉보호보다 믿고 기다려 주는 게 중요하다고 했어요.
examples.en: The teacher said trusting and waiting matters more than overprotecting.

explain: 주로 부모가 아이에게 '과잉보호를 하다', 아이가 '과잉보호를 받다'로 써요. '오냐오냐 키우다'는 뭐든 들어줘서 버릇없게 키운다는 느낌이라 조금 달라요.

phrases.example: 부모가 과잉보호를 하면 아이가 혼자 해 보기 어려워요.
phrases.en: If parents overprotect, it's hard for the child to try things alone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 보호하는 쪽, 보통 부모의 입장에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the one protecting, usually the parents.

phrases.example: 과잉보호를 받고 자란 친구는 결정을 잘 못 해요.
phrases.en: My friend who grew up overprotected has trouble making decisions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 보호받는 쪽, 보통 아이의 입장에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the one being protected, usually the child.

phrases.en: Please don't overprotect your child too much.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-하다'를 붙여서 동사로 짧게 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-하다' makes it a short verb.

explain_en: It mostly appears as '과잉보호를 하다' for parents and '과잉보호를 받다' for the child. '오냐오냐 키우다' means giving in to everything and spoiling a child, so it feels a bit different.

t90.ax: I grew up overprotected, so I'm easily scared.

examples.en: I had a small quarrel with a friend.

examples.ko: 다툼 때문에 하루 종일 기분이 안 좋았어요.
examples.en: I was in a bad mood all day because of the quarrel.
We ended the quarrel and apologized to each other.
Even between a couple there are quarrels.
The police came because of the dispute with a neighbor.
Let us stop talking before it turns into a quarrel.

explain: '다투다'의 명사형이에요. 말이나 의견으로 맞설 때 어울리고, 몸으로 치고받는 일은 보통 '싸움'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: A small quarrel came up with my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다툼이 일어났다고 말할 때 가장 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural phrase for saying a quarrel broke out.

phrases.en: I had an argument with my friend yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '다툼'의 기본 동사로, 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The base verb of 다툼, used more often in daily speech.

phrases.en: I want to avoid a quarrel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 싸우고 싶지 않다는 마음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you don't want to fight.

explain_en: It is the noun form of 'datuda'. It fits a clash of words or opinions; a physical fight is usually called 'ssaum'.

examples.ko: 화가 나도 사람에게 막말하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Even when you are angry, you should not say harsh things to people.
That person speaks rudely to anyone.
I regret saying harsh things to my brother yesterday.
I apologized right after saying those harsh things.
Many people throw rude remarks at each other in the comments.
I spoke rudely to my parents and got scolded badly.

explain: 화가 나서 거칠게 말하는 모습에 쓰고, 욕설이 없어도 상대를 무시하는 말투면 막말이라고 해요. '험담'은 없는 데서 흉보는 것이라 달라요. 뉴스에서는 '막말 논란'처럼 명사로도 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I was angry and said harsh things to my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '막말하다'를 둘로 나눠서 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common way of splitting 막말하다 into two parts.

phrases.example: 그 정치인의 막말 논란이 뉴스에 나왔어요.
phrases.en: The controversy over that politician's rough remarks was in the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 누군가의 거친 말이 문제가 될 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in the news when someone's rude words become an issue.

phrases.en: Don't speak carelessly to your friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각 없이 거칠게 말하는 모습에 쓰고, 막말하다보다 조금 부드러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes speaking roughly without thinking; a little softer than 막말하다.

explain_en: It describes talking harshly out of anger; even without swear words, a dismissive tone counts as 막말. '험담' is speaking ill of someone behind their back, which is different. In news the noun appears often, as in '막말 논란'.

examples.ko: 어부가 새벽에 배를 타고 바다로 나갔어요.
examples.en: The fisherman went out to sea by boat at dawn.
My grandfather worked as a fisherman when he was young.
The fishermen are tidying up their nets.

examples.ko: 그 섬 마을 사람들은 대부분 어부예요.
examples.en: Most people in that island village are fishermen.
I bought fresh fish directly from a fisherman.

examples.ko: 태풍 소식에 어부의 가족들이 걱정이 많아요.
examples.en: With the typhoon news, the fishermen's families are very worried.

explain: 고기 잡는 일을 직업으로 하는 사람이에요. 낚시를 취미로 하는 사람은 '낚시꾼'이라고 해서 구분해요. 요즘은 '어민'이라는 말도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: Many fishermen live in the seaside village.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어부와 비슷하지만 어촌에 사는 사람 전체를 가리킬 때가 많고 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close to 어부, but it often refers to people who live by fishing in general, and it is common in the news.

phrases.en: Fishermen get up early in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 명을 말할 때 '-들'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -들 when talking about more than one person.

phrases.en: The fisherman's boat came back to the port.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '의'를 붙여 어부가 가진 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding the particle 의 shows that something belongs to the fisherman.

explain_en: It means a person who fishes for a living. Someone who fishes as a hobby is a 낚시꾼, so the two are distinguished. Nowadays 어민 is also widely used.

examples.en: My account went into the minus.
The temperature dropped to minus five degrees.
This month the business is at a loss.

examples.ko: 급할 때를 위해 마이너스 통장을 만들었어요.
examples.en: I opened an overdraft account for emergencies.
That is not a disadvantage for us.
The calculation came out negative.

explain: 반대말은 '플러스'예요. 숫자 앞에 붙는 '-'뿐 아니라 돈이 모자라는 것, 손해, 도움이 안 되는 일에도 비유로 써요.

phrases.en: overdraft account
phrases.nuance_ko: 통장에 돈이 없어도 정해진 한도까지 빌려 쓸 수 있는 통장이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An account that lets you borrow up to a set limit even with no balance.

explain_en: Its opposite is 플러스. Besides the "-" sign before a number, it is used figuratively for a shortage of money, a loss, or something unhelpful.

examples.en: I got overcharged at a restaurant in a tourist area.
In peak season, overcharging for lodging is serious.

examples.ko: 바가지요금인 줄 알았으면 안 샀을 거예요.
examples.en: If I had known it was a rip-off price, I wouldn't have bought it.

examples.ko: 바가지요금은 미리 가격을 물어보면 피할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can avoid rip-off prices by asking the price beforehand.

examples.ko: 바가지요금에 화가 나서 가게 주인에게 따졌어요.
examples.en: I was angry at the rip-off price and argued with the shop owner.

examples.ko: 바가지요금 때문에 휴가 기분이 다 망쳤어요.
examples.en: The inflated price ruined my whole vacation mood.

explain: 물건이나 서비스의 값이 정상보다 터무니없이 비쌀 때 써요. 보통 관광지, 택시, 성수기 숙박처럼 손님이 사정을 잘 모르는 상황에서 말해요. '바가지요금을 당하다/물다'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 시장에서 물건을 샀다가 바가지를 써서 속상해요.
phrases.en: I bought something at the market and got ripped off, which upsets me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비싼 값을 속아서 내게 되었을 때 말해요. 반대로 상대가 그렇게 할 때는 '바가지를 씌우다'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said when you were tricked into paying too much. When the seller does it to you, it is '바가지를 씌우다'.

explain_en: It is used when the price of goods or services is absurdly higher than normal. It is typically said in situations where the customer doesn't know the going rate, like tourist spots, taxis or peak-season lodging. Common patterns: '바가지요금을 당하다/물다'.

examples.en: Gas prices went up, so fuel costs a lot.
With an electric car, you hardly worry about fuel costs.
In winter, the burden of heating fuel costs is big.

examples.ko: 한 달 연료비를 계산해 보니 십만 원이에요.
examples.en: I calculated a month of fuel costs and it's 100,000 won.
The company covers fuel costs for business trips.

examples.ko: 연료비는 차가 클수록 더 많이 나와요.
examples.en: The bigger the car, the higher the fuel cost.

explain: '기름값'은 일상에서 주유할 때 편하게 하는 말이고, '연료비'는 차뿐 아니라 난방·운송 같은 비용 전체를 말할 때도 써요. '연료비가 들다', '연료비를 아끼다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: I drove less and saved on fuel costs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비용을 줄였다고 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for saying you cut costs.

phrases.en: In winter the burden of fuel costs gets bigger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈이 많이 들어서 힘들다는 느낌을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds the feeling that the cost is a heavy burden.

phrases.en: Gas prices are too expensive these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주유소에서 내는 돈을 편하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual word for what you pay at the gas station.

explain_en: '기름값' is the casual word for the price of gas when you fill up, while '연료비' can also cover costs for heating or transport in general. Typical phrases are '연료비가 들다' and '연료비를 아끼다'.

en: financial difficulty; stringency of capital; lack of funds

examples.en: The company closed because of a shortage of funds.
I heard the shop is having cash trouble.
Many small businesses suffer from a lack of funds.
The construction stopped halfway due to a funding shortage.
To solve the cash shortage, they borrowed money from a bank.
The funding crunch got so bad that even employees' pay was delayed.

explain: 회사나 가게 같은 곳의 운영 돈이 모자랄 때 써요. 개인 이야기라면 '돈이 없다', '쪼들리다'가 더 자연스러워요. '취업난', '구인난'처럼 '-난'이 붙은 말과 같이 기억하면 좋아요.

phrases.en: The company stopped work because of a lack of funds.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자금난'과 뜻이 비슷하지만 어려움보다 돈이 모자라다는 사실에 가까워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to the headword, but states the lack of money more than the hardship.

phrases.en: The shop suffered from a lack of funds for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오랫동안 돈 때문에 힘들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone struggles over a long time because of money.
phrases.en_equiv: to suffer from a funding crunch

phrases.en: We solved our funding problem by taking out a loan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈 문제를 풀었다고 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for saying a money problem was solved.

explain_en: Lack of operating money, esp. for businesses. It is used when a company or shop runs short of operating money. For an individual, '돈이 없다' or '쪼들리다' sounds more natural. It helps to learn it with other '-난' words such as '취업난' and '구인난'.

t90.ax: I heard the shop is having cash trouble.

examples.en: There are many low-wage jobs, so life is hard.

examples.ko: 저임금으로 일하는 사람도 최저임금은 꼭 받아야 해요.
examples.en: Even people who work for low wages must get at least the minimum wage.

examples.ko: 저임금 때문에 젊은 직원들이 회사를 떠나요.
examples.en: Young employees leave the company because of low pay.
Many young people are struggling with low pay.

examples.ko: 공장에서 저임금 노동자를 구한다는 공고가 났어요.
examples.en: A notice went up that the factory is looking for low-wage workers.
If low wages continue, spending drops too.

explain: 반대말은 '고임금'이에요. 일상에서는 '월급이 적다'라고 하고, 저임금은 뉴스나 경제 이야기에서 더 많이 써요. '최저임금'은 법으로 정한 가장 낮은 금액이라서 뜻이 달라요.

phrases.en: Support is needed for low-wage workers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 월급이 적은 노동자를 가리키는 뉴스식 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A news-style term for workers who earn little.

phrases.en: Many young people suffer from low wages.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낮은 월급 때문에 힘든 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes hardship caused by low pay.

phrases.en: Competition for high-wage jobs is tough.
phrases.nuance_ko: 저임금의 반대말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 저임금.

explain_en: The opposite is '고임금'. In daily talk people say '월급이 적다', while 저임금 appears more in news and economic discussion. '최저임금' is the legal minimum amount, so it means something different.
